responsibility: This module implements the Rust frontend’s name-resolution subsystem in GCC, turning parsed Rust ASTs into bindings between uses and definitions across the language’s separate value, type, label, and macro namespaces. Its main responsibilities span crate-level orchestration, scope and rib management, canonical-path construction, duplicate and unresolved-name diagnostics, import and glob handling, and the multi-pass traversal needed by Rust’s rules: older AST resolver files perform a two-pass collect-then-resolve walk over items, statements, expressions, patterns, paths, struct fields, and types, while the newer Resolver2_0 files split the work into top-level collection, early macro-oriented resolution, import finalization, and late ordinary name lookup built on persistent namespace stacks and a shared resolution context. Supporting files provide the core resolver state, per-scope rib semantics, persistent ForeverStack scope graphs, read-only access to finished results for later phases, assignment-target validation during expression resolution, and a small custom ICE finalizer, making this directory the frontend stage that establishes Rust lexical/module visibility and namespace meaning before later semantic analysis and lowering.
